definition: A reward model trained to score outputs according to a defined set of principles, used within a Constitutional AI-style training pipeline.
details: Constitutional reward models formalize principle-based preferences into a trainable signal, extending the Constitutional AI approach beyond self-critique into the reward modeling stage of alignment training.
story: Picture a parachute packed by a second pair of hands: nobody plans to need it, but everyone is glad it was checked. The idea is simple: before something powerful is let loose, someone checks that it will not do real harm to real people. It is the habit of asking, before every launch, what could go wrong — and then doing something about it. Caution is not the enemy of progress — it is the reason progress gets to keep going. And that is Constitutional Reward Model — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
